newsitem.title: USA: MEMC Electronic sees possible Q4 loss.
newsitem.headline: MEMC Electronic sees possible Q4 loss.

text.p: MEMC Electronic Materials Inc said on Thursday it may post a loss in the fourth quarter, with sales expected to be about $200 million.

"(W)e believe sales for the fourth quarter will be sequentially lower, in the range of $200 million with a resulting decrease in operating profit," said Ludger Viefhues, chief executive officer. "The bottom line could reflect a slight loss."
MEMC, which produces silicon wafers, reported revenues of $262.38 million in the fourth quarter of 1995. Silicon wafers are used in semiconductors.

MEMC said the inventory correction in the worldwide semiconductor industry led to increased order cancellations, which the company said it has been unable to fully replace. MEMC said it has cut operating costs and delayed equipment expenditures, where appropriate.
The company reported third quarter 1996 earnings fell to $0.51 a share from $0.71 last year. Sales for the quarter totalled $303.53 million versus $251.21 million.
MEMC company officials could not be reached for further details on the possible fourth quarter loss.

Marketing, administration and technology expenses increased to 10.7 percent of net sales for the third quarter of 1996 compared to 9.3 percent last year, but were slightly lower than for the second quarter of 1996, MEMC said.
Operating profit margin was 11.2 percent for the third quarter of 1996 compared to 15.7 percent for the period last year.
In addition, MEMC said the effective tax rate for the 1996 third quarter was 40.0 percent compared to 39.6 percent for the quarter in 1995.
Gross margin decreased to 21.9 percent for the 1996 third quarter compared to 25.0 percent for the quarter last year and 28.0 percent for the 1996 second quarter, MEMC said.
The decrease in gross margin was the result of a lower rate of capacity utilization and start-up and training costs, partially offset by sales mix improvements, it said.
"We continue to be optimistic about the longer term prospects of the silicon wafer industry," Robert Sandfort, president and chief operating officer of MEMC, said in a statement.
"We believe our investments in technology and strategic capacity expansions are important in maintaining and enhancing our leadership position in this industry," he said.
